Which State is the best place overall to live in the South? Which is the worst? Why?
None. All stupid, all fat. Stay away.

I have lived in FL, Atl, Biloxi, Houston area, and a few places in the middle of the country. I have had extended visits in 49 states (2-3 weeks at a time, sometimes months) over the past 20+ years for work.

What type of information are you looking for exactly?

Just wanted to know about some of the differences between Southern states when it comes to lifestyle, culture and whatnot. I feel like Texas is sort of considered the de-facto leader of the Southern states, though I might be wrong.

Texas pretty much has anything you want - low taxes, less governmental interference (the Texas legislature only meets for a month once every 2 years), best Mexican food in the states, 5 large metro areas each with its own features, cheap cost of living (low property values, low food prices, cheap gasoline, no income tax), 400+ miles of beaches, every type of ecology except arctic. Lots of Spanish speakers, and most of the metros are more a collection of neighborhoods than a homogeneous "city." Best parking spots aren't the ones closest to the building, it's the ones in the shade due to the high heat.

Louisiana - if you like the outdoors and don;t mind getting your feet wet, this is the place. Only 1 metro area of note (sorry, Baton Rouge and Shreveport), but they have legal gambling/casinos, and pretty lax laws. Roads suck, though. Cajun cooking is amazing, small towns are either great or shitty, and very segregated.

Mississippi - Biloxi/Gulfport area is nicer than the rest of the state. School system is a joke, unless in really nice neighborhoods in the Jackson or Hattiesburg area. Great place to be a redneck - hunting/fishing/carousing - without the issue of getting your feet wet just from standing on the ground like in LA. You have the river casinos up by Memphis, and those in Biloxi along the Gulf. Jefferson Davis was from here, and there used to be a museum about the Old South in his estate in Gulfport along the coast - if it survived Katrina. Like New Orleans, lots of crime in the cities. Suburbs are the way to go here. Southern Mississippi has Cajun food, further up it becomes more Southern.

Alabama - I can't say anything bad about Alabama - Huntsville is home to the most PhD's per capita due to Redstone and Marshall being there (think missiles and rocket scientists). Tuscaloosa is a nice mid-sized city, I have family there. You have 2 major universities in Auburn and U of A. Mobile has some really bad areas, like most cities, but I would rather be in a bad area of Mobile or Montgomery than in a bad area of Chicago, Baltimore, or Detroit. Better like college football. Southern cooking reigns here, some Cajun style filters in from further West, along the coast. Big army base on the GA line.

Georgia - one major city. Great airport. City - stay in the suburbs, although their are areas gentrifying and coming back - Buckhead, for example. Center of population is up north of the city (Alpharetta, Tucker, Norcross, etc.) o many companies are putting their offices there. Traffic is a bear, and you better drive fast. You have mountains in the north of the state (Helena) and the beaches and islands on the Atlantic coast are a well-kept secret. Savannah is a beautiful old town with charm to match a New orleans, without the crime. Great universities - Georgia Tech is a top school, U of G, Emory, and Ga. Southern in Statesboro for the budget-conscious. CDC is based there, so if the pandemic apocalypse happens, you have the best shot of surviving. Swamp fishing down south, beaches, mountains, and urban areas make this an interesting state for outdoors activities. Nice amusement park in Atlanta (Six Flags) and another touristy area out around Stone Mountain.

Florida - Up there with Texas. Many major metros to choose from. Beaches/coast is never more than 1 hour away. Swamps, waterways are the choices for outdoor activities. Traffic is bad in the winter with all the snowbirds. Beware of sinkholes. Property values are higher than other states, but still a bargain compared to others. No income taxes here, either. Food prices are higher here, but have more local fresh options than other states. Great place to own property for renting/income, due to the large number of visitors.

South Carolina - Haven't been here much - Greenville mostly. Have heard great things about Charleston, but have never been. You have the coastal areas - Hilton Head, Myrtle Beach, etc. for the tourists. Greenville has a nice little downtown area and things to do on weekends during the summers. Also some good universities (USC, Clemson), and the food is a mix of Southern and coastal / seafood.

North Carolina - One major metro and quite a few mid sized areas. Charlotte is big and new and shiny, but is becoming Atlanta as the suburbs move farther away from the city center. Raleigh-Durham-Chapel Hill area boasts some great universities and is called the "Research Triangle" area. Great place to live - cost of living is low, lots of hills and trees. Beautiful area. Go further west and you run into the Smoky Mountains past Asheville, which is another gorgeous old town. You have beaches and water sports out east, and hills and mountains out west. Great hiking.

Tennessee - Smoky Mountains to the east and tapers down to the Mississippi river to the west. Lots of options here, 3 metro areas to choose from. I prefer Knoxville because I like hiking, but Nashville is nice, too, but geared toward tourism, IMO. High tax state, though. Memphis is a disaster of a city. But the suburbs is nice. Good universities, UT, Vanderbilt, U of Memphis (but don't live too far away from campus), and nice culture. Maryville-Alcoa area by Knoxville airport is one of my favorite places - quiet, right at the western entrance to Smoky Mountain National Park, great hiking, clean air, etc. Outside the inner cities, the spaces in between are filled with nice people, a bit redneck, but not as bad as Mississippi or Alabama rural areas. Great hunting and fishing, great lakes, great hiking.

Arkansas - upper Ark is a bass fisher's paradise with Bull Shoals/Table Rock. Hot Springs is a bit dirty for me, but it's a fun dirty. Little Rock is the only real metro, and it hit or miss for neighborhoods. NW Arkansas is Wal-Mart country, and the U of Ark is up there, too. Lots of natural resources here, and it's a relatively low cost, low populated state.

Hope these help a bit.
